Description:en: A surgically created connection between an artery and a vein, usually in the arm, used as the preferred long-term vascular access for hemodialysis.
A synthetic tube surgically placed between an artery and a vein to provide vascular access for hemodialysis when an arteriovenous fistula is not suitable.
A long-term central venous catheter inserted under the skin and into a large vein to provide vascular access for hemodialysis.
A temporary central venous catheter inserted directly into a large vein for immediate or short-term hemodialysis access.
A catheter surgically inserted into the peritoneal cavity to facilitate peritoneal dialysis by allowing dialysate to enter and leave the abdomen.
Indicates the type of access currently being used by the patient to perform dialysis. This may be a vascular access for hemodialysis or a peritoneal access for peritoneal dialysis.
A bicarbonate-buffered dialysate commonly used for routine hemodialysis to correct metabolic acidosis and remove waste products.
